name: New York City - Local Law 26 of 2016 and NYC Digital Accessibility

laws.summary: City agencies must make a reasonable effort to make their websites accessible, and the City must report on progress.

policy_docs.title: NYC.gov Website Process - Creating Accessible Content

applies_to: NYC.gov and all City agency websites and digital content.

deadlines.what: Federal ADA Title II date for NYC (population 50,000+).

exceptions: The City adopted the five exceptions from DOJ's Title II rule.
requires: WCAG 2.2 Level AA for agency websites and content
Website accessibility statement and a way to report barriers (Website Accessibility Feedback Form)
Digital Accessibility Coordinator at MOPD trains agencies and writes the Local Law 26 Digital Accessibility Reports
mobile: not addressed on the pages reviewed - Title II's mobile app requirement applies regardless.
procurement: Not stated on the pages reviewed.
enforcement: Internal (MOPD coordinator, public reports); federal Title II enforcement and private suits.
notes: A vendor article mentions an NYC 'Local Law 12' on digital accessibility; not verified against Legistar and not included. The Local Law 26 legistar PDF URL is from search results (the 2016 local laws compilation), not opened. Agency 5-year accessibility plans come from search summaries (likely Local Law 12 of 2023 accessibility plans), unverified.
